We welcome the consensus on a mechanism to appoint the president of higher national elections commission following delays in implementing the previously agreed upon mechanism. We look forward to reaching consensus on all other outstanding matters. Third, reaching an understanding on the mechanism to organize elections does not necessarily mean their success or their actual holding. We need a real breakthrough and this requires prioritizing Libya's interests and the interests of its people over any other interests or considerations while implementing concrete and pragmatic steps within clear time frames. The Kingdom stresses that the Libyan people remain the primary victims of this continued competition among different actors. We look forward to ending the successive prolonged transitional phases which have turned into a vicious circle. Thus, the Kingdom underlines the need for all parties to put the future of Libya and the security of its people and their prosperity above all other interests. They must work seriously to ensure the success of all initiatives aimed at resolving Thank you, Madam President.

I thank the representative of Bahrain for the statement. I shall now make a statement in my capacity as the representative of Denmark. Let me start by thanking Ezerzgi Tete for her briefing and welcome the representative of Libya to our meeting today. Let me also give a special thanks to Ms. Nisabek for bringing her perspectives to the Council, including on the adverse impact of climate change on the lives and security of the Libyan people. I will make three points. First, as we've heard, it's one year since the UNSMIL roadmap was launched. Denmark continues to support the UN-led mediation efforts, and we commend the efforts of SISG Chadde to this end. We urge Libyan political stakeholders to narrow their differences and put the interests of the people first. In this vein, we welcome the progress made in the small group convenings. Denmark encourages the parties to redouble their efforts to complete the first two milestones of the roadmap to create the conditions for holding national elections. Further, The recommendations of the structured dialogues reflect the aspirations of Libyans for a stable and prosperous state with effective governance. We encourage Libyan political leaders to implement them. Second, Denmark is concerned about the volatile security situation in Libya. Unresolved political deadlock hampers unified state security control. This was clear in the recent armed clashes, which endangered civilians and damaged critical infrastructure, including Severia refinery. Denmark strongly condemns these clashes. We call for de-escalation and stress the need for all actors to refrain from further violence. Effective measures to protect civilians in accordance with international humanitarian law and human rights law must be taken. Third and finally, As Ms. Beck clearly outlined, Libya faces growing climate related risks, including water scarcity and rising temperatures. When combined with weak infrastructure and institutional fragmentation, climate pressures can have a devastating impact on livelihoods and prosperity. These risks must therefore be factored into peacebuilding, conflict prevention, and local mediation efforts. We urge the international community to support the Libyan authorities in addressing these challenges, to strengthen resilience and translate climate commitment into action. As we've heard, this will have a clear impact on the lives of the people of Libya. I thank you. I resume my function as President of the Council, and I now give the floor to the representative of Libya.

Thank you, Madam President. At the outset, I wish you all the luck during the Presidency of the Council in this month. I would also like to thank Mrs Hanna Tete for her briefing. We took note of all what was mentioned. We would also like to thank Ms Nisa for her briefing, which expresses the opinion of a large part of the people who have been suffering for years. have been frustrated from such meetings and all they want are pragmatic concrete results. Therefore, before we deliver our statement, we must reiterate once again that holding such meetings must be accompanied by a real will to break this vicious circle of political effort. We have to overcome the traditional approaches and move towards concrete measures that would meet the aspirations of the Libyan people for stability, Libya must be lifted from the scourge of Chapter 7 to put an end to all those chapters. This is a shared responsibility on all our shoulders. Ladies and gentlemen, we commend the progress that was announced by the Special Representative in her briefing today and all the arrangements reached between the two main parties in the 4+4 committee. This was achieved in a relatively short time during the negotiations over the past two months on consensus on the draft laws for the presidential and parliamentary elections and the mechanism to appoint the president of the High National Electoral Commission. We stress that such laws are not an end in themselves. Instead, they are the only tool that would empower the Libyan people to exercise their right to choose their leader. and shape their institutions. No political track can be legitimate without being based on the voice of the people. We reiterate the need to respect all national initiatives and dialogues that respond to the aspirations of the Libyan people. They have to result in a direct and not interpretable way to an end of all transitional phases. It has to come through fair and free elections, through just laws that do not exclude anyone and are applicable. We welcome any constructive international effort to support the national dialogue and put an end to the divisions, but it has to be Libyan owned and Libyan led complementary to the UN framework and the decisions of the relevant Security Council resolutions. We underlined that the Libyan ownership of the political process must not be just a slogan that is repeated without being reflected in practical terms, although the Libyan people do care for the ownership of their political decision, but the amount of international interference in the Libyan process has had its impact on so many levels. Therefore, there is a need for an international role that supports the national will, not instead of. It must support the Libyan institutions, not overcoming them. The Libyan ownership must move from an announced principle to a practical implementation that respects the right of the Libyan people to decide on the future of their country. Ladies and gentlemen, under such exceptional circumstances in Libya. We appreciate all international effort to support the economic path and the unification of the budget, as well as the unified development programme. However, we must now investigate the reasons behind the non-implementation following nine months since the signing of the agreement and the timetable of the implementation, we find that it is dangerous that there are still challenges obstructing the implementation. Adjusting this file can no longer be delayed. It is a national priority to respect the Libyan dinar and safeguard our monetary process from any dangers. In this vein, and to ensure the success of such agreements, we call upon everyone to support the independence of the Central Bank of Libya to ensure its prerogatives legally and financially away from any political pressures. It is high time for this agreement to be implemented. It has to be announced to the public and state institutions, especially the auditing institutions, to ensure the transparency, accountability and commitment of all to its provisions. The deterioration of the basic services provided to the citizens, as we have heard from Mrs. Nisa today, and the continued livelihood crises, foremost the energy and power crises, is no longer linked to technical matters or lack of resources. It is also linked to the corruption networks and the smuggling, trafficking of of the oil. These are dangerous crimes that have devastating consequences on equal footing to criminal problems. Therefore, even though we welcome the decision of the sanctions committee on the 22nd of July, but how can the international community accept the designation of one ship while there are entire fleets that smuggle our oil before the eyes of the international community? We call upon this Council and the sanctions committee to move with determination to ensure the accountability of all entities and networks and their supporters locally and internationally without selectivity, for they are known to all in this Council. Such steps and others will ensure transparency and accountability on the revenues of oil and other marketing contracts, as was stated in the reports of the experts. In the same vein, We welcome the adoption by the sanctions committee on the 6th of June, their agreement that allows the Libyan Investment Authority to retain the revenues of the Libyan frozen assets. This is what we have asked for time and again, to preserve the money and treasure of the Libyan people that are depleted. It is unacceptable that the Libyan money will remain in foreign banks that are benefiting from it and are also taking huge revenues while their real value is being depleted due to inflation. This is structured theft that we will not allow. Talking about sanctions, we would like to recall once again that it is necessary to lift the names of many Libyans that for years have no reason to be designated, whether they are representatives of the old regime or others. It's not acceptable that such names will remain on the designation list, we have to also look into the humanitarian side of such cases. We call upon the international community to support all military tracks, dialogue and security meetings that garner all security and military representatives. We believe that such contact is a real safeguard against the fall into confrontations that cost the Libyan people a lot. The Government of National Unity continues to implement a progressive plan to adjust the military and security situation. It is the strategy that started in 2021 based on a practical approach towards the current arrangements. We are trying to guide their work in line with the needs of the government and its institutions. and ensure restructuring and reformulation of different battalions to ensure the protection of the citizens and its structures. We have moved through different tracks, through measures that have put an end to certain arrangements or the tasks that no longer meet the needs of the state, in addition to other paths that would ensure redirecting and regarding the capabilities in line with the state capabilities. In this vein, we condemn and strongly reject the political assassination approach or reliance on violence in any way, as well as the targeting of critical state institutions and oil institutions. These are dangerous steps that beg the question, what are the agendas adopted that would only push the country towards a vicious circle of violence? The Libyan people have suffered for years from violence and assassinations. These people look for courageous steps that would unify our military under one united civilian authority, preventing the use of weapons that would only fall in the hands of the state and refrain from any foreign military presence on our country. Permanent security will only be achieved by ending all other military actions that are unlawful. Because this is the cornerstone to ensure political settlement and its protection. To conclude, we reiterate that the strategic importance of Libya must not be undermined in its resources and oil reserve, it expands to its location and role in ensuring international trade, the security of oil and other matters. Therefore, protecting Libya and its coastal and its coast will ensure the stability of the Middle East and the paths of trade between Africa and Europe. As we have mentioned time and again, all what has been mentioned related to divisions or challenges on any files, especially when it comes to the Libyan citizen, whether economically, humanitarily, or on the security sphere, are only symptoms because we have not yet reached a fundamental and comprehensive political solution based on diversity and real democracy, a solution based on a constitution and a state of institutions and law that has its unified military and has full control over weapons to defend the people. This continued struggle for years came due to different foreign interferences. This crisis was used for particular proxy wars and specific agendas. And the proof is before your eyes in so many other countries. Therefore, we call upon you once again for positive international partnership. a partnership on equal footing that respects the will and sovereignty of the Libyan people. We would like to thank all countries who have adopted such approach, and we hope that others will follow and adjust their policies so that benefit would be for all. History will record that, and the Libyans will remember that. Thank you, Madam President.

I thank the representative of Libya for the statement. There are no more names inscribed on the list of speakers. I now invite Council members to informal consultations to continue our discussions on the subject. The meeting is adjourned.
